$comment: Simplest case. Parking policy dominates here: traffic is sparse enough that idle car position matters more than assignment cleverness. Not a speed negative control — see notes; the hydraulic car does reach its 0.63 m/s rated speed inside one 3.0 m floor pitch.
name: Garden Apartments
notes: THIS BUILDING COLLAPSES THE DISPATCHER MENU, and the collapse is real rather than a defect - so it is measured here rather than tuned away. At the shipped configuration (trafficProfile residential, typical 5% of population per 5 min, rise-and-fall, 26-28 legs in the window) 8 of the 78 ordered dispatcher pairs are bit-identical ON THE LEGS at every one of five seeds 20260810-14: eta = fairness-first, collective = collective-enroute, and capacity-aware, auction, auction-multi-round and destination-eta mutually. At three seeds the count is 12 of 78, which is the same fact measured with a weaker identity test - a pair needs one differing decision at one seed to separate, so the count falls as seeds are added and MUST be quoted with its seed count. Under evening-egress the window holds 6 legs and 36 of 78 pairs coincide. The cause is trace thinness, not structure: hold the building and the profile fixed and raise only the arrival rate and the count goes 8 (3%), 8 (5%), 1 (7%), 3 (10%), 3 (15%), 0 (20%) at five seeds, and every pair separates at 78 legs. A player who picks 'Contract-net auction, multi-round' here and gets a byte-identical run to 'Capacity aware' has met this and not a bug.

NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO FIX THAT, which is why it is not fixed. The menu only fully separates at 20% of population per 5 min, three times the residential profile's own declared maximum of 7% and four times its typical - so no data-legal setting of this building separates it, and reaching one would mean either fabricating an arrival rate CIBSE does not support, or inventing residents. 120 people over five floors of 24 is already a dense garden block, and the sparseness is this building's PURPOSE: the $comment above says parking policy dominates here precisely because traffic is too thin for assignment cleverness to matter. A small residential building genuinely has little traffic. What is owed is a label on the screen where the player meets it, not a bigger number in this file.

Passenger transfer time uses the residential value, 1.75 s per passenger per direction — luggage, strollers, carts (ISO 4190-6). It is resolved from the building type: elevator-specs.json -> timing.passengerTransferS.residential. Neither car overrides it, so if a car here ever reports 1.2 s, the type is not reaching the car and the round trip is understated by about 5 % (the Phase 2 gate found exactly that).

CORRECTED, and it was wrong in the other direction: this building is NOT a speed negative control. At v = 0.63 m/s, a = 0.6 m/s^2, j = 0.8 m/s^3 the jerk-limited profile reaches rated speed after about 1.14 m of travel (v^2/a alone is 0.66 m), so a 3.0 m floor pitch is spent mostly at rated speed and the hop is speed-limited, not acceleration-limited. Verified with packages/core/src/physics/motion: a single-floor hop takes 6.562 s at 0.63 m/s and 5.417 s at 1.00 m/s, and the modelled round trip at 8 passengers falls from 124.9 s to 111.1 s, an 11 % improvement. Raising ratedSpeedMps here helps, and a test that expected it not to would be pinning a bug.

Speed does stop paying beyond about 1.6 m/s, and for the stated reason rather than the claimed one: at 1.6 m/s the car needs roughly 5.5 m to reach rated speed, so single-floor hops become jerk- and acceleration-limited (5.285 s, barely better than 1.00 m/s) even though the 15 m express run keeps improving (25.6 s to 12.8 s). The floor pitch sets the threshold, so quote the threshold, not a blanket claim.

The real speed negative control in this repository is Midtown Office: 2.5 m/s against a 3.8 m pitch needs about 8.05 m to reach rated speed, so a single-floor hop never gets there at all (4.678 s, peaking at 1.63 m/s) and is unchanged by raising rated speed to 4 m/s.
